summary.text: Patient 1, aged 59 at index surgery with BMI 22.7 kg/m^(2) and ASA grade 1, had left breast cancer at clinical stage cT4N2, and received neoadjuvant chemotherapy.

The index operation was MRM with pedicle TRAM flap; sentinel lymph node biopsy was not done and axillary dissection was done, with operating theatre duration 368 min and total number of LN taken 20. A surgical drain was placed intraoperatively.

Chyle leak was detected at POD 3, the drain stayed in for 28 days with total drain output 1,234 mL, and management was dietary consultation plus high-protein, low-fat diet. No recurrence of chyle and no other complications were recorded.

summary.text: Patient 4, aged 67 at index surgery with BMI 24.7 kg/m^(2) and ASA grade 3, had right breast cancer at clinical stage cT2N0. The index operation was Simple mastectomy with SLNB followed by AD; sentinel lymph node biopsy was done and axillary dissection was done, with operating theatre duration 209 min and total number of LN taken 14. A surgical drain was placed intraoperatively.

Chyle leak was detected at POD 225 and POD 332, the drain stayed in for 10 days with total drain output 538 mL, and management was dietary consultation plus low-fat diet. No recurrence of chyle and no other complications were recorded. A persistent, recurrent seroma needed repeated drainage, 6 times in total.

Because the leakage was persistent, lymphoscintigraphy showed lymphatic leakage over the right axilla, and surgical exploration with plication under ICG guidance was done at POD 426. The patient remained well with no evidence of seroma recurrence after the surgery.

summary.text: Patient 7, aged 41 at index surgery with BMI 19.8 kg/m^(2) and ASA grade 2, had left breast cancer at clinical stage cT2N1. The index operation was Skin-sparing MRM with implant expander insertion; sentinel lymph node biopsy was not done and axillary dissection was done, with operating theatre duration 195 min and total number of LN taken 16. A surgical drain was placed intraoperatively.

Chyle leak was detected at POD 5, the drain stayed in for 13 days with total drain output 751 mL, and management was dietary consultation plus MCT diet. No recurrence of chyle and no other complications were recorded.

Table 3 summary cell says seroma requiring drainage in 4/7 (57.14%) and none in 3/7, but only three patient cells (patients 2, 4 and 6) describe seroma drainage and the text says three patients required additional drainage; N/A cells are not recorded as absent.
Text says the median body weight was 22.2 kg/m^(2), which is the BMI median in Table 1; BMI is recorded from the table.

Text groups mastectomy types (3 simple with SLNB, 2 simple with SLNB then AD for positive frozen-section nodes, 2 modified radical) in counts that do not line up one to one with the Table 1 rows, so the frozen-section indication is not assigned to individuals.

Cohort statements (median age, tumour quadrant, axillary metastases by FNAC, ER/PR status, resolution in 3 to 11 days, maximum daily chyle output) have no literal mapping to individual patients and are not copied.
Dash cells in the Premorbid and Neoadjuvant therapy rows are not recorded as absent items.
Table 1 Premorbid rows 2 and 3 are flattened in the segment text; the raw table row and column spans place them deterministically under patients 3 and 5, so those items are included.
Text (b00039) reports bilateral pedicle latissimus dorsi flaps for one patient, while Table 1 lists a pedicle LD flap without laterality for patient 5; the bilateral detail is not assigned.
